# harborpilot_subscription_entitlement (Resource)

Subscription terms of an account: fee, period and known usage windows.

Changes made outside Terraform are detected on refresh and shown as a diff of `spec`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "harborpilot_subscription_entitlement" "max" {
  name = "claude-max-alice"
  spec = jsonencode({
    account_id = harborpilot_provider_account.claude_alice.id
    plan_name  = "Max"
    fee        = "100"
    currency   = "USD"
    period     = "monthly"
    starts_on  = "2026-01-01"
    windows = [
      { name = "five_hour", seconds = 18000, unit = "percent" },
      { name = "seven_day", seconds = 604800, unit = "percent" },
    ]
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name (lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`).
- `spec` (String) The subscription entitlement specification as JSON, usually written with `jsonencode({...})`. See the `EntitlementSpec` schema in the Harbor Pilot API reference. Properties you leave out are sent as their zero value (empty string, list or map, `0`, `false`), except `enabled`, which must be set.

### Read-Only

- `drift_state` (String) `drifted` when the object was changed outside Terraform since Terraform last wrote it.
- `id` (String) Stable object id.
- `managed_by` (String) Source of the last change (`terraform` after an apply).
- `revision` (Number) Server revision, used for optimistic concurrency.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by id or by name.
terraform import harborpilot_subscription_entitlement.example <id-or-name>
```
